title: Route requests and fail over streamed responses

blocks.text: Failover is safe before nonempty output; after output begins, switching providers would splice responses. The task is: Fail over between supplied provider(request)->chunk-iterator callbacks. A RuntimeError before any NONEMPTY emitted chunk permits trying the next provider; after any output return a terminal partial-stream error, never concatenate another provider's answer. Return collected chunks, attempt log, and status. This deterministic core treats RuntimeError as retryable; provider selection/billing are external.

The inputs are `providers`, `request`. Keep their roles separate while you trace the solution. The animation follows the supplied implementation, so every highlighted operation connects to code you can inspect.

Before following the implementation, identify the output's shape and meaning. Then identify which input values can affect one selected output. This gives you a testable mental model before the code adds implementation detail.
What changes in the boundary case

Change one input at the edge of the stated contract and trace where the behavior changes. Use the Trace control to switch between the normal path and this boundary focus. The algorithm does not get permission to invent an unstated fallback.

A useful test changes one condition while holding the remaining inputs fixed. Compare the output shape, state transition, valid edges, selected tokens, or returned status. This isolates the reason for the change.
